announcements.text: LATA-CTI JV LLC,* Albuquerque, New Mexico (FA8903-26-D-0062); Los Alamos Technical Associates Inc.,* Albuquerque, New Mexico (FA8903-26-D-0063); TEPA-Weston JV,* Kansas City, Missouri (FA8903-26-D-0065); A&M-BERS JC LLC* Tulsa, Oklahoma (FA8903-26-D-0067); North Wind Site Services LLC, Idaho Falls, Idaho (FA8903-26-D-0068); Browngrul-A&M JV, Tulsa, Oklahoma (FA8903-26-D-0075); GSIA-Parsons JV LLC, Flemington, New Jersey (FA8903-26-D-0076); B-2 JV LLC, Saint Paul, Minnesota (FA8903-26-D-0077); Migo-A&M JV LLC, Tulsa, Oklahoma (FA8903-26-D-0078); Plexus CDM Smith JV LLC, Alexandria, Virginia (FA8903-26-D-0079); EA Engineering Science, Technology Inc. PBC, Hunt Valley, Maryland (FA8903-26-D-0084); EarthCreek LLC, Atmore, Alabama (FA8903-26-D-0085); HydroGeoLogic Inc., Reston, Virginia (FA8903-26-D-0086); Environmental Chemical Corporation, Burlingame, California (FA8903-26-D-0087); Paragon Professional Services LLC, Anchorage, Alaska (FA8903-26-D-0088); Insight Tidewater LLC, Brea, California (FA8903-26-D-0070); Noreas Inc., Irvine, California (FA8903-26-D-0071); Enviro-Terra Noreas LLC, Laguna Hills, California (FA8903-26-D-0072); Koman Remediation Solutions LLC, Anchorage, Alaska (FA8903-26-D-0073); Ahtna Solutions LLC, Anchorage, Alaska (FA8903-26-D-0074); Brice Integrated LLC, Anchorage, Alaska (FA8903-26-D-0059); Kemron Environmental Services Inc., Atlanta, Georgia (FA8903-26-D-0056); Cape-SRS JV LLC, Norcross, Georgia (FA8903-26-D-0058); Bhate Environmental Associates Inc., Birmingham, Alabama (FA8903-26-D-0055); RSI Remediation LLC, San Francisco, California (FA8903-26-D-0080); Lakota-Sundance JV LLC, Sitka, Alaska (FA8903-26-D-0081); Tanaq-ECM JV3 LLC, Anchorage, Alaska (FA8903-26-D-0060); FPM-AECOM JV3, Oneida, New York (FA8903-26-D-0061); Ayuda SERES JV LLC, Lafayette, Colorado (FA8903-26-D-0064); Navarro Research and Engineering Inc., Oak Ridge, Tennessee (FA8903-26-D-0066); Eastern Shawnee-Trevet JV LLC, Overland Park, Kansas (FA8903-26-D-0069); Aerostar SES LLC, Knoxville, Tennessee (FA8903-26-D-0082); Engineering/Remediation Resources Group Inc., Martinez, California (FA8903-26-D-0057); Gold Wave Inc., Beaufort, South Carolina (FA8903-26-D-0083) were awarded a maximum $3,500,000,000 firm-fixed-price, cost-plus-fixed-fee, cost-reimbursable, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity, multiple award task order contract for environmental optimization and construction services. This contract provides for the full range of methods, technologies, and supporting activities for environmental construction, demolition, restoration, and remediation efforts. Work will be performed at various locations across the United Sates and is expected to be completed by September 2034. These contracts were competitive small business set-aside acquisitions, and thirty-five offers were received. Fiscal 2026 operation and maintenance funds in the amount of $3,000 per awardee will be obligated upon awarding the first task order. The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron, Joint Base San Antonio Lackland, Texas, is the contracting activity.

PTC Inc., Boston, Massachusetts, has been awarded a $99,767,830 modification (P00013) to a previously awarded contract (FA8109-21-C-0001) for Air Force Enterprise Supply Chain Analysis, Planning, and Execution. The modification brings the total cumulative face value of the contract to $194,830,400 from $95,062,570. Work will be performed at Boston, Massachusetts, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, and Tinker Air Force Base, Oklahoma, and is expected to be completed by Sept. 28, 2031. Working Capital Funds in the amount of $19,893,542 are being obligated at time of award. The Air Force Sustainment Center Tinker Air Force Base, Oklahoma, is the contracting activity.

KAL Architects Inc., Irvine, California, has been awarded a $25,000,000 indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity, firm fixed‐price contract, for architect and engineering Services. The contract provides for the design of various projects and engineering studies. Work will be performed at Edwards Air Force Base, California; and Air Force Plant 42, Palmdale, California; and is expected to be completed by Sept. 22, 2031. This contract was a competitive acquisition, and sixteen offers were received. Fiscal 2026 operation and maintenance funds in the amount of $257,286 are being obligated at the time of award. The Air Force Test Center, Edwards Air Force Base, California, is the contracting activity (FA9301‐26‐D‐0012).

Segue, Arlington, Virginia, was awarded a 17,167,724 Firm-fixed-price contract for Manpower Programming and Execution System. This contract provides for the comprehensive modernization and DevSecOps integration for the Manpower Programming and Execution System, including its strategic migration to the cloud, to ensure its continued reliability as the authoritative data source for Total Force authorizations. Work will be performed at Arlington, Virginia, and is expected to be completed by March 29, 2030. This contract was a sole source acquisition. Fiscal 2026, 3400 O&M Funds in the amount of $5,188,389 are being obligated at time of award. The Air Force District of Washington at Headquarters Air Force, is the contracting activity (FA7014-26-F-0239). (Awarded on Sept 22, 2026).

L3Harris Technologies Inc., Salt Lake City, Utah, is awarded an $876,440,942 cost-plus-incentive-fee, undefinitized modification (P00021) to previously awarded contract (N0001924C0061). This modification adds scope to provide for the continued development of the Next Generation Jammer Low Band system, including non-recurring tooling and equipment and associated labor; delivery of system demonstration test article pods; additional cybersecurity and system security development; and product, logistics, test and evaluation, and software support for the Navy and Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF). Work will be performed in Salt Lake City, Utah (43%); Hollywood, Alabama (14.8%); Lansdale, Pennsylvania (8.1%); Clifton, New Jersey (8%); Boulder, Colorado (7.5%); Goleta, California (5.8%); Australia (3.4%); Carlsbad, California (3%); Edgewood, New York (2.6%); Waco, Texas (2.6%); Parsippany, New Jersey (1%); and Long Island, New York (0.2%), and is expected to be completed in fiscal 2031. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation (Navy) funds in the amount of $3,653,866; and RAAF cooperative funds in the amount of $23,044,630 will be obligated at the time of award. This modification was not competitively procured. Naval Air Systems Command, Patuxent River, Maryland, is the contracting activity.

Massa Products Corp.,* Hingham, Massachusetts, is awarded a $61,819,998 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for the design, manufacture, test, package and delivery of DT-574 Hydrophones. This contract includes an ordering period of five years. Work will be performed in Hingham, Massachusetts, and is expected to be completed by September 2031. Fiscal 2026 national sea-based deterrence funds in the amount of $1,066,993 will be obligated on the first delivery order immediately following award of the basic contract, of which, none will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was competitively procured via SAM.gov, with multiple offers received. Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division, Newport, Newport, Rhode Island, is the contracting activity (N66604-26-D-X600).

Bird-Johnson Propeller Company, LLC, Walpole, Massachusetts, was awarded a $56,065,687 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for propeller inspection and repair services in support of the Navy 2SCOG Program. Work will be performed in Walpole, Massachusetts, and is expected to be completed by September 2031. Fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance, Navy funds in the amount of $564,837 will be obligated at the time of award and will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was competitively procured via SAM.gov, with two offers received. Naval Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, is the contracting activity N64498-26-D-1031. (Awarded Sept. 21, 2026).

InSynergy Engineering, Inc., Honolulu, Hawaii is awarded a $49,000,000 firm-fixed price indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for architect-engineer (A-E) services. This contract provides for fire protection engineering projects at various locations under the cognizance of Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC), Pacific; but may also include work worldwide. Work will be performed at various Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, and other government facilities within the NAVFAC Pacific area of responsibility (AOR), including but not limited to Guam (75%), Hawaii (10%), Tinian (5%), Australia (5%), Other Pacific Ocean area (2%), Diego Garcia (1%), Japan (1%), and Korea (1%). The term of the contract is not to exceed 60 months with an expected completion date of August 2031, or until all task orders have been completed. Fiscal 2026 Military Construction (MILCON) funds in the amount of $10,000 are obligated for the minimum guarantee of this award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. Future task orders will be primarily funded by military construction funds. This contract was competitively procured via the SAM.gov website, with seven offers received. NAVFAC Pacific, Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam, Hawaii is the contracting activity (N62742-26-D-1210).

Systems Planning & Analysis Inc. of Alexandria, Virginia is awarded a cost-plus-fixed-fee Task Order (N0003026F6001) with a value $48,295,159 under contract (N00030-25-D-3019). This value includes optional line items. The effort will include engineering and technical studies, assessments, and management support for Navy's Conventional Prompt Strike and Future Regional Deterrence programs. Work will be performed in Washington, DC (63%); Huntsville, Alabama (9%); Bangor, Washington (9%); Alexandria, Virginia (6%); Cape Canaveral, Florida (5%); Denver, Colorado (4%); Albuquerque, New Mexico (4%). Work is expected to be completed on Sept. 29, 2031. Fiscal 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) funding in the amount of $604,337 and fiscal year 2026 Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation, Navy (RDT&E, N) in the amount of $400,000 will be obligated at time of award. No funds will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This Task Order will be awarded as a sole source acquisition with the authority of 15 U.S. Code 638 Research and Development and was previously synopsized on the System for Award Management (SAM.gov) online portal. Strategic Systems Programs, Washington, District of Columbia, is the contracting activity. The information contained in the announcement is unclassified.

VACCO Industries, South El Monte, California, is awarded $16,844,319 for a fixed-price contract with economic price adjustment for the procurement of thirty-one hovering and depth control (HDC) press valves and eleven HDC vent valves for use on Navy Virginia-class submarines. The contract does not contain an option provision. All work under the contract will be performed in South El Monte, California, and is expected to be completed by May 2032. Fiscal 2026 working capital funds (Navy) representing 75% of the contract's total ceiling price in the amount of $12,633,239 will be obligated at time of award and those funds will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. One company was solicited for this sole-source requirement pursuant to the authority set forth in 10 U.S. Code 3204 (a)(1) and one offer received. Naval Supply Systems Command Weapon Systems Support, Mechanicsburg, Pennsylvania, is the contracting activity (N00104-26-C-ZA30).

Bristol Design Build Services LLC,* Anchorage, Alaska (W912BV-25-D-0043); Sea Pac Engineering Inc.,* Los Angeles, California (W912BV-25-D-0042); Southwind Construction Services LLC,* Edmond, Oklahoma (W912BV-25-D-0041); Gideon Contracting LLC,* San Antonio, Texas (W912BV-25-D-0040); and Ross Group Construction Corp. LLC, Tulsa, Oklahoma (W912BV-25-D-0039), will compete for each order of the $495,000,000 indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity, firm-fixed-price contract for design-build and design-bid-build vertical construction projects. Bids were solicited via the internet with five received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of July 24, 2030. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Tulsa, Oklahoma, is the contracting activity. (Awarded July 25, 2025).

Walsh Construction Co. II LLC, Chicago, Illinois, was awarded a firm-fixed-price contract for construction of a bypass channel including an approximately 3,900-foot-long and 300-foot-wide channel with a floodwall and an earthen levee. The amount of this action is $141,515,713 with a total cumulative face value of $169,431,703. Bids were solicited via the internet with 10 received. Work will be performed in Fort Worth, Texas, with an estimated completion date of March 21, 2029. Fiscal 2022 civil construction funds in the amount of $141,515,713 were obligated at the time of the award. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Fort Worth, Texas, is the contracting activity (W9126G-26-C-A034).

GMHILL-Native Solutions JV LLC, Winnebago, Nebraska, was awarded a $107,591,250 indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity, firm-fixed-price contract to provide sustainment, renovation, and modernization construction. Bids were solicited via the internet with five received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of Sept. 22, 2031. U.S. Army Field Directorate Office, Fort Sam Houston, Texas, is the contracting activity (W5168W-26-D-A037).

Georgia Vocational Rehabilitation Agency, Tucker, Georgia, was awarded a $28,538,445 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for full food services, including dining facility management, food receiving and storage, food preparation and serving, remote site feeding, and facility sanitation. Bids were solicited via the internet with seven received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of Sept. 22, 2031. U.S. Army Field Directorate Office, Fort Sam Houston, Texas, is the contracting activity (W5168W-26-D-A036).

ZAPATA Black & Veatch JV LLC, Charlotte, North Carolina, was awarded a $21,795,885 firm-fixed-price contract for architect and engineering services for the Modernized Pre-Mix and Nitrocellulose Dehydration Facility at the Radford Army Ammunition Plant. Bids were solicited via the internet with four received. Work will be performed in Radford, Virginia, with an estimated completion date of March 16, 2028. Fiscal 2026 ammunition procurement, Army funds in the amount of $21,795,885 were obligated at the time of the award. U.S. Army 419th Contracting Support Brigade, Fort Drum, New York, is the contracting activity (W911S2-26-C-A003).

BCI Construction USA Inc.,* Pace, Florida, was awarded a $13,950,019 firm-fixed-price contract for lock and dam hydraulics upgrades. Bids were solicited via the internet with three received. Work will be performed in Coraopolis, Pennsylvania, with an estimated completion date of Sept. 29, 2028. Fiscal 2025 and 2026 civil operation and maintenance funds in the amount of $13,950,019 were obligated at the time of the award. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, is the contracting activity (W911WN-26-C-A010).

Norfolk Dredging Co., Chesapeake, Virginia, was awarded an $11,213,334 modification (P00003) to contract W91278-26-C-A015 for additional maintenance dredging and disposal. The modification brings the total cumulative face value of the contract to $56,955,071. Work will be performed in Irvington, Alabama, with an estimated completion date of June 11, 2027. Fiscal 2026 Civil operation and maintenance funds in the amount of $11,213,334 were obligated at the time of the award. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Mobile, Alabama, is the contracting activity.

Steele's Garage Door Repair LLC,* Richland, Washington, was awarded a $10,660,972 firm-fixed-price contract for non-personal facilities maintenance and services for overhead doors including comprehensive operations, preventive and corrective maintenance, and facility management for an estimated inventory of 3,512 commercial and automated doors. Bids were solicited via the internet, with nine received. Work will be performed in Fort Hood, Texas, with an estimated completion date of March 24, 2032. Fiscal 2026 other procurement, Army funds in the amount of $1,939,663 were obligated at the time of the award. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers' Engineering and Support Center, Huntsville, Alabama, is the contracting activity (W912DY-26-C-A065). (Awarded Sept. 21, 2026).

Minuteman Security Solutions LLC,* Lorton, Virginia, was awarded a $9,972,000 indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity, firm-fixed-price contract for continued deployment, integration, and fielding services supporting the Integrated Commercial Intrusion Detection System-Five program. One bid was solicited with one received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of Sept. 22, 2029. U.S. Army Contracting Command, Aberdeen Proving Ground, Maryland, is the contracting activity (W909MY-26-D-A001).

C.E. Niehoff & Co., Evanston, Illinois, has been awarded an estimated $94,987,708 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for High Mobility Multipurpose Wheeled Vehicle engine accessory generators. This was a sole-source acquisition using justification 10 U.S. Code 3204 (a)(1), as stated in Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302-1. This is a five-year contract with no option periods. The ordering period end date is Sept. 23, 2031. Using military service is Army. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 through 2031 Army working capital funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Weapons Support, Warren, Michigan (SPRDL1-26-D-A001).

Gaylord Chemical Co. LLC, Covington, Louisiana, has been awarded an estimated $46,633,330 commercial firm-fixed-price requirements contract for the manufacture, purification, blending, analysis, packaging and supply of specification-grade hypergolic propellants. This was a competitive acquisition with one response received. This is a four-year 11-month base contract with one five-year option period and one six-month extension. Location of performance is Alabama, with a Sept. 14, 2031, performance completion date. Using customers are Air Force, Space Force, Navy, War Department, Missile Defense Agency and federal civilian agencies. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 through 2031 defense working capital funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Energy, Joint Base San Antonio, Lackland, Texas (SPE601-26-D-1531).

UPDATE: Dentsply North America LLC, Charlotte, North Carolina (SPE2DF-26-D-0020, $49,500,000) has been added as an awardee to the multiple award contract for dental supplies and equipment for the Defense Logistics Agency Electronic Catalog, issued against solicitation (SPE2DE-25-R-0002) and awarded Feb. 12, 2026. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

General Electric Co., Lynn, Massachusetts, has been awarded a maximum $39,926,265 firm-fixed-price, one-time buy delivery order (SPRTA1-26-F-0288) issued against a basic ordering agreement (SPE4A1-22-G-0010) for J85 air compressor cases. This was a sole-source acquisition using justification 10 U.S. Code 3204 (a)(1), as stated in Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302-1 (a)(2). The delivery order completion date is Sept. 30, 2031. Using military service is Air Force. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 defense working capital funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Weapons Support, Oklahoma City, Oklahoma.

Triumph Gear Systems Inc., Park City, Utah, has been awarded a maximum $23,943,876 firm-fixed-price contract for pylon conversion actuators. This was a sole-source acquisition using justification 10 U.S. Code 3204 (a)(1), as stated in Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302-1 (a)(2). This is a three-year contract with no option periods. The performance completion date is Sept. 30, 2029. Using military service is Navy. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 through 2029 Navy working capital funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Weapons Systems Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (SPRPA1-26-C-VA72).

AAR OEM Distribution – Defense, Wood Dale, Illinois, has been awarded a maximum $18,138,960 firm-fixed contract for V-22 spare parts. This was a sole-source acquisition using justification 10 U.S. Code 3204 (a)(1), as stated by Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302-1. This is a three-year four-month contract with no option periods. The performance completion date is Jan. 12, 2030. Using military service is Navy. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 through 2030 Navy defense working capital funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Weapons Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (SPRPA1-26-C-XA13).

The Northrop Grumman Systems Corp., Melbourne, Florida, has been awarded a maximum $10,762,018 firm-fixed-price delivery order (SPRPA1-26-F-D601) issued against a five-year basic ordering agreement (SPRPA1-26-G-D601) for mission control displays. This was a sole-source acquisition using justification 10 U.S. Code 3204 (c)(1), as stated in Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302-1. This is a three-year contract with no option periods. The delivery order end date is Feb. 9, 2029. Using customers are Navy and foreign military sales to France. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 through 2029 Navy working capital funds and foreign military sales funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Weapons Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

Weibel Equipment Inc.,* Reston, Virginia, has been awarded a maximum $12,130,705 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for muzzle velocity radar systems and containers. This was a sole-source acquisition using justification 10 U.S. Code 3204 (a)(1), as stated in Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302-1. This is a three-year contract with no option periods. The performance completion date is Sept. 21, 2029. Using military service is Army. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 through 2029 Army working capital funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Weapons Support, Warren, Michigan (SPRDL1-26-D-0062). (Awarded on Sept. 21, 2026).

Carver Pump Co., Muscatine, Iowa, has been awarded a maximum $10,983,000 firm-fixed-price contract for centrifugal pumps. This was a sole-source acquisition using justification 10 U.S. Code 3204 (a)(1), as stated in Federal Acquisition Regulation 6.302-1. This is a one-year contract with no option periods. The delivery order end date is June 12, 2028. Using military service is Navy. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 Navy working capital funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Weapons Support, Mechanicsburg, Pennsylvania (SPRMM1-26-P-MD51). (Awarded on Sept. 21, 2026).
